subject: geography
title: Cold Environments: Alaska & Antarctica 🧊

concepts.def: US state with oil reserves at Prudhoe Bay.
1,287 km oil pipeline built on stilts above permafrost.
Arctic Alaska oilfield — largest in North America.
1959 pact — Antarctica for peaceful science only.
1991 ban on mineral mining in Antarctica.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Prudhoe Bay oilfield was discovered in 1968.

The Trans-Alaskan Pipeline (built 1977):
• 1,287 km long
• Built on stilts to protect permafrost
• Allows caribou to pass underneath

Brings jobs and revenue but ecological risks.

Drawbacks include:

• Exxon Valdez spill 1989 — huge damage
• Disruption to caribou migration
• Impact on Inuit way of life
• Boom-bust economy

Trade-off between economy and environment.

Antarctica is uniquely protected:

• Antarctic Treaty 1959 — peaceful science only
• Madrid Protocol 1991 — bans mining for 50 years
• IAATO regulates tourism
• No permanent population

A model of international cooperation.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the tundra and the taiga biomes?
options: Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.
Tundra and taiga are the same biome with different names.
Tundra is treeless cold biome (too cold and permafrost-dominated for trees), while taiga (boreal forest) is the band of coniferous forest just south of the tundra in subarctic latitudes.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.

mcqs.q: How is the dependency ratio calculated?
options: (Population aged 0-14 plus population aged 65+) divided by population aged 15-64, multiplied by 100 — comparing dependants to the working-age population.
The dependency ratio is the number of unemployed people in a country.
Tundra is in the Arctic and taiga is in the Antarctic.
The dependency ratio is the number of children per family.
